procedure: Traced membership removal, guest offboarding, principal disablement and last-steward recovery separately.
Compared the D7/C2/P9/G3/K8 migration example with existing dataset, grant, credential, immutable release and migration-lock contracts.
Walked concurrent removal, stale move approval, lost transfer response and policy-replication failure scenarios; checked F02.2 is the single migration owner.
Integration review corrected the issuer-offboarding example to emergency disablement and confirmed migration extends the existing principal table.

acceptance.criterion: Define an audited last-steward transfer/recovery path and distinguish removal of one membership from full principal disablement.
acceptance.evidence: ADR 003 Offboarding operations; Last steward and emergency recovery

acceptance.criterion: Describe how existing curator/dataset/API-credential records migrate without widening access, losing attribution or orphaning data.
acceptance.evidence: ADR 003 One migration authority and D7 example

acceptance.criterion: Specify expected generations, idempotency/conflict behavior and how policy changes enter the later independent recovery journal; identify the single migration authority.
acceptance.evidence: ADR 003 Generations, concurrency and idempotency; Independent policy journal contract

negativeCases: Disabling the last steward cannot be blocked by the ordinary stewardship invariant.
A revoked legacy credential remains revoked after migration.
A historical curator field cannot bypass new disablement or stewardship transfer.
A stale move approval or changed idempotency payload cannot commit.
Old independently signed policy without a current trusted checkpoint cannot reopen a restored service.
limitations: Contract only; F02.2 owns the actual migration and F03/F04 enforcement.
Actual recovery approvers and durability objectives remain SITE01 decisions.
Independent policy replication and closed-service restore qualification remain O03.
